issues.description: The endpoint fast-space comparison is only sketched. It reuses the starting-bin threshold gamma_Q for paths that end in a common bin V, and relies on the all-subinterval rate comparison on [n-L,n]. The argument appears correct, since the rates are full-segment rates and the gap margin is above 2g for every witness from U, but it is stated briefly. I flag it as a presentation-level thin spot, not as a gap.
issues.evidence: 'In particular, (exterior-rate-comparison) applies on each [n-L,n] with the same full-segment rates, so the singular-value comparison and the backward argument just proved compare their fast spaces at n.'

coverage: Read all 7 sections of the LaTeX in full, plus the README. Checked: the dyadic chord lemma (midpoint displacement, the L2 convolution bound, and the square-summability); the Markov constant in Prop good-frames (4*alpha^2/b^2 <= eta/400); the scale hierarchy (B=b^{1/8}, g=b^{1/2}, L~b^{1/4}n, Bn >= n^{79/80}); finite-interval splitting (the triangular-product counting, the shear recurrence and its sign/q cases, and the Gram-determinant volume identity); the threshold selection with candidates (1+8j)g; the singular-subspace comparison; the relative exterior perturbation bound (the e^{sigma m+a}(C eps e^{a-sigma})^q algebra); the switching construction (weighted boundary inverse, the K_+ and K_- graph bounds, contraction radii Q_k*delta -> 0 and Q_k*r/delta -> 0, the linear and nonlinear switch error o(r), the Laplace expansion of the four determinants, the exact cancellation in the permutation determinant identity, label recovery and injectivity via uniqueness, and the change of variables giving Phi_*(rho|G) <= 2rho); the word construction (symplectic transitivity giving uniform marginals, the sublist atom bound, the multigraph degree argument for the distance bound, the likelihood ratio 2^{2KN}, and recomputed log F_i, log E_i, log T_i with the 0.47*eps*l term and the growth induction); the recognition lemma for offsets that are and are not divisible by m_i; the rate lemma and divergence of sum K_i R_i^16; zero entropy, ergodic selection and standardness; the aligned-law and parent-slot uniformity; the window-entropy numerics (.9995*.9988 > .996); the graph-window exception 2D-2 residues; cheap scales (negation of the limit is handled correctly, |J_i| >= K_i/32); the heavy-light symplectic graph bound (theta <= .055, beta_L -> 0, total .62); symbol matching (3*kappa, Markov 600*kappa/d* < .03, mass .96); phase recovery; entry pairing; and the final .912 > .62 contradiction.
main_claim: There is an ergodic invertible zero-entropy transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space that is not measurably conjugate to any C^infinity diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density on a compact manifold of any finite dimension, including nonorientable manifolds and manifolds with boundary.
